title: How do we find angle a in four figures?
description: Four figures show parallel lines with one angle marked a in each. Interior angles, a corresponding angle with a linear pair, a split angle and a right angle each give a, and a closing check adds each answer to its partner.
teaching_notes: One idea: in each figure, name the relation between a and a given angle, then add up or take away. Watch for angles that are shown but not needed.

video_script.why: The child uses interior angles, corresponding angles and linear pairs of the solved example in four new figures.
video_script.substitution: the book's own four figures, each with parallel lines and one angle marked a
video_script.anchor: four small figures with parallel lines, each with one angle marked a and one or two given angles
video_script.payoff_line: Each angle came from a straight line, a right angle or a parallel line rule

final_answer.spoken: in the first figure eigh is one hundred and thirty eight degrees, in the second it is one hundred and eighteen degrees, in the third it is one hundred and five degrees, and in the fourth it is twenty three degrees

maths_rules: interior angles on the same side add up to 180, so a = 180 - 42 = 138 and the 100 is not needed
the corresponding angle of 62 is 62, and a is a linear pair of it, so a = 180 - 62 = 118
the rest of 110 is 110 - 35 = 75, which is the corresponding angle next to a on a straight line, so a = 180 - 75 = 105
67 and a fill a right angle, so a = 90 - 67 = 23
video_script.design: Four small figures in a row. In each, the angle a takes the colour of the relation used, and the closing check shows each answer beside its partner.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four small figures with parallel lines, each with an angle marked a

marks.scene: the title card From your book arrives
marks.fig: the four figures are drawn in a row, each with an angle marked a
marks.ask: a question mark rests beside a in every figure

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about angles between parallel lines.
<bookmark mark='fig'/>There are four figures, and each has a marked angle eigh.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the angle eigh in each figure.

beats.on_screen: the four figures stay on the board with question marks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two parallel lines with a transversal; two angles between the lines on the same side glow with 180° and the words interior angles; two angles side by side on a straight line glow with 180° and the words linear pair

marks.int: two angles between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal glow and the words interior angles are written
marks.sum: 180° is written beside the interior angles
marks.lin: two angles side by side on a straight line glow and the words linear pair are written, with 180° beside them

beats.colours: the two relations have two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='int'/>Angles between parallel lines, on the same side of a transversal, are called interior angles.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>They add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='lin'/>Two angles side by side on a straight line are called a linear pair. They add up to one hundred and eighty degrees too.

beats.on_screen: Given: four figures with parallel lines and an angle marked a; some angles shown are not needed

marks.given: the given line is written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four figures with parallel lines and one angle marked eigh.
Some angles that are shown are not needed.

beats.on_screen: To find: the angle a in each figure

marks.find: the question is written under the given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find eigh in each figure.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: first figure, a and 42° are interior angles on the same side, so a = 180° − 42° = 138°; the 100° is not needed

marks.int: in the first figure, a and 42° glow as interior angles on the same side
marks.book: the solved example of the book appears for a moment beside the figure
marks.take: 180 − 42 is written and a is marked 138°

narration: <bookmark mark='int'/>Step one, in the first figure, eigh and forty two degrees are interior angles on the same side.
<bookmark mark='book'/>This is the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='take'/>The angle eigh is one hundred and eighty take away forty two. That is one hundred and thirty eight degrees.
<bookmark mark='extra'/>The one hundred degrees is not needed.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: second figure, the corresponding angle of 62° is 62°, and a is a linear pair of it, so a = 180° − 62° = 118°

marks.corr: in the second figure, an arrow goes from 62° to its corresponding angle, marked 62°
marks.pair: that angle and a glow as a linear pair
marks.take: 180 − 62 is written and a is marked 118°

narration: <bookmark mark='corr'/>Step two, in the second figure, the corresponding angle of sixty two degrees is sixty two degrees.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>The angle eigh makes a linear pair with it.
<bookmark mark='take'/>The angle eigh is one hundred and eighty take away sixty two. That is one hundred and eighteen degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: third figure, the rest of 110° is 110° − 35° = 75°, the corresponding angle next to a, so a = 180° − 75° = 105°

marks.rest: in the third figure, the 110° angle is shown split, with 35° and the rest
marks.sub: 110 − 35 is written and the rest is marked 75°
marks.next: an arrow goes from the rest to the corresponding angle next to a, marked 75°
marks.take: 180 − 75 is written and a is marked 105°

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step three, in the third figure, the one hundred and ten degrees contains thirty five degrees.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>The rest is one hundred and ten take away thirty five. That is seventy five degrees.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The rest is the corresponding angle of the angle next to eigh on a straight line. That angle is seventy five degrees.
<bookmark mark='take'/>The angle eigh is one hundred and eighty take away seventy five. That is one hundred and five degrees.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: fourth figure, 67° and a fill a right angle, so a = 90° − 67° = 23°

marks.right: in the fourth figure, 67° and a glow inside a right angle
marks.take: 90 − 67 is written and a is marked 23°

narration: <bookmark mark='right'/>Step four, in the fourth figure, sixty seven degrees and eigh fill a right angle. A right angle is ninety degrees.
<bookmark mark='take'/>The angle eigh is ninety take away sixty seven. That is twenty three degrees.

marks.one: 138 + 42 = 180 is written beside the first figure
marks.two: 118 + 62 = 180 is written beside the second figure
marks.three: 105 + 75 = 180 is written beside the third figure
marks.four: 23 + 67 = 90 is written beside the fourth figure

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step five, to check, one hundred and thirty eight and forty two make one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='two'/>One hundred and eighteen and sixty two also add up to one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>One hundred and five and seventy five do the same.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Twenty three and sixty seven add up to ninety.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed on the board
marks.one: a is filled in as 138° and 118° in the first two figures
marks.two: a is filled in as 105° and 23° in the last two figures

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each angle came from a straight line, a right angle or a parallel line rule.
<bookmark mark='one'/>In the first figure eigh is one hundred and thirty eight degrees. In the second it is one hundred and eighteen degrees.
<bookmark mark='two'/>In the third it is one hundred and five degrees. In the fourth it is twenty three degrees.
